title: Patchwave weeklong rollout canvas and annotated release notes (2027-09)
content:
Purpose and scope:
Patchwave is a small-batch deployment to adjust model-routing heuristics, KV-cache prefetch tuning, and a safety throttle for low-memory nodes. This doc is the working weeklong canvas: quick preflight checklist, day-by-day rollout calendar (progression plan and watchlist), operator cues and rollback triggers, plus an annotated draft of the user-facing release notes.

Context / motivation:
- Motivation: reduce tail latency for long-chat sessions (>=1024 tokens) by shifting a small fraction of traffic to a low-latency quantized variant and enabling a more aggressive prefix cache prefetch window.
- Risk profile: moderate (stateful caches, cross-node routing). Expected user-visible improvements for <5% of sessions; potential regression risk in KV persistence during aggressive prefetch.
- Target audience: internal infra and platform teams, SRE on-call, partner-facing CS if customer SLAs are affected.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Start: Monday 09/06 - gradual 3-phase canary across region-us-east-1 -> region-eu-west-1 -> global.
- Progression: day-by-day percent targets (1%, 5%, 20%, 50% then 100% over 6 working days).
- Rollback: automated circuit at latency P95 > 250ms for 15min or error rate delta >= 1.5x baseline for 10min. Manual rollback if data store KV misses spike > 10% (investigate/hotfix).

Preflight checklist (must be green before morning-of start):
- [ ] All unit and integration tests for model-router and cache-manager merged and green on main (GH PR 2891).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created: patchwave-latency-p95, patchwave-error-rate, kv-miss-rate, routing-fallback-count. Dashboards link: Confluence:Patchwave-Design-2027.
- [ ] Canary infra: reserve 4 GPU nodes in us-east-1 with preloaded quantized model (Dedicated pool: patchwave-canary-01).
- [ ] Smoke automation: smoke-test script runbook verified (smoke/prefetch-check.sh) and on-call has SSH keys.
- [ ] Rollback artifacts: warm image with previous routing logic available (ami: rwd-release-2027-07-22), rollback playbook reviewed by SRE.
- [ ] Legal & security: no PII changes; config change only. Compliance ack from security (email thread).
- [ ] Communication: release Slack channel #release-patchwave created; calendar invites for daily 12:30 sync (15m). Notify CS for customers with >1M tokens/day usage.

Day-by-day rollout calendar (high-level):
Monday 09/06 - Canary week start (US)
- 09:00: preflight check list walk (owners: Ava + Jordan)
- 10:00: push routing change to canary cluster (initial fraction = 1% traffic)
- 10:15–12:30: monitor telemetry (P95, error-rate), run smoke tests against warm nodes
- 12:30: 15m sync: decision to continue or rollback (go/no-go criteria below)
- Afternoon: if green, bump to 5% in late afternoon (18:00) and snapshot telemetry baseline.

Tuesday 09/07 - Canary expansion (US + EU)
- 02:00: automated gradual expansion to eu-west-1 at 1% (overnight ops window)
- 10:00: target 5% in both regions; run integration with routing fallbacks and KV persistence checks
- 12:30: convene ops sync; verify kv-miss rate < 3% absolute delta vs baseline

Wednesday 09/08 - Broader pilot
- Target 20% global across non-critical traffic lanes (exclude enterprise-tier for first pass)
- Run targeted evals using synthetic long-chat prompt sets from RED-4188 to validate quality regressions
- Night: snapshot logs and prepare for 50% bump tomorrow if green

Thursday 09/09 - Surge window (50%)
- Morning: bump to 50% for daytime window; ensure autoscale headroom and throttle limits are active
- Continuous watch for tail latency spikes and routing fallback loops (watch: routing-fallback-count)
- 12:30: checkpoint; if green, schedule full roll to 100% Friday morning

Friday 09/10 - Full roll (100%) or rollforward decision
- 03:00: progressive roll to 100% on low-traffic window
- 08:00: global verification of P95 latency and embedding pipeline health
- 12:30: final release sync, confirm release notes and customer comms draft

Saturday-Sunday - Stabilization window (monitor only, no config changes)
- On-call monitors with reduced surface area; capture anomalies for Monday retro

Operator cues, canary gating, and rollback triggers (automated + manual):
Automated circuit-breakers (must be configured before start):
- If P95 latency for the patchwave variant > 250ms AND > 1.3x baseline for 15 minutes -> auto-revert routing for 10 minutes and page SRE
- If overall 5xx rate increases by 1.5x baseline for 10 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous routing logic and notify #sre-oncall
- If KV-miss-rate increases by > 10% absolute -> pause cold-prefetch and trigger manual review (do not proceed to next traffic step)

Manual escalation triggers (ops must decide within 20 mins):
- Repeated routing-fallback loops (>100 in 30m)
- Customer-facing errors reported by CS for enterprise customers
- Any evidence of persistent state corruption in cache (investigate, can escalate to rollback)

Notes to on-call / runbook snippets (copy into pager):
- How to force revert: playbook: ./ops/revert_patchwave.sh --ami rwd-release-2027-07-22 --scale-down-delay 120
- How to inspect prefetch behavior: run `curl localhost:7000/debug/prefetch?session=<id>` on canary node
- Log grep quick checks: `rg "patchwave" /var/log/serving/runtime | tail -n 200`

Observability checklist (prepped dashboards & alerts):
- Latency: patchwave-p95 (green < 200ms, amber 200–250ms, red > 250ms)
- Errors: patchwave-5xx-rate (alert at 0.5% absolute increase)
- KV: kv-miss-rate (alert if >5% from baseline) and kv-write-latency
- Routing: fallback-count, route-imbalance-by-node
- Cost: per-token CPU/GPU minutes per model variant (spot check)

Release notes (annotated draft) - internal -> external slicing:
Short summary (one-liner):
- "Patchwave: improved long-chat latency and smarter prefix caching for lower tail latency in multi-turn sessions. Rollout begins 2027-09-06."

What changed (user-facing):
- Model routing: a selective traffic shift routes long-chat sessions to a tuned quantized variant under low-latency paths. Expected P95 latency improvement of ~10–25% for sessions >1024 tokens.
- Caching: increased prefix prefetch window which reduces remote KV fetches for multi-turn flows (config toggle: prefetch.window=48).

Notes for developers (more technical):
- Endpoints: /api/generate unchanged; internal routing occurs in service router v2.4.8 (non-breaking).
- New flags: RUNTIME_PREFETCH_WINDOW, ROUTER_QUANT_THRESHOLD (defaults preserved).
- Rollout plan: staged canary across regions; enterprise-tier exclusion possible via feature flag.

Known issues and constraints (ship note):
- Rare KV miss spike observed in internal load tests when prefetch window is aggressive; we have a throttle guard that will pause prefetch if miss-rate spikes. Ops: watch kv-miss-rate closely.
- Short-term cost increase for ~3–5% of sessions as they are routed to quantized variant with heavier CPU decode.

Customer impact and comms plan:
- Proactive: email to enterprise customers with >1M tokens/day 24h before full rollout. Include opt-out instructions (contact CS).
- Reactive: CS playbook in Confluence with suggested messaging and rollback ETA (approx 30–45 min).

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- [ ] Should we include apac regions in initial pilot? (ops capacity question; default: no)
- [ ] Confirm cost attribution for quantized variant to billing pipeline (finance).
- [ ] Add synthetic canary that replays top-100 long-chat prompt sets to verify quality drift daily for first week. Owner: Priya.

Post-release retro agenda (recommended):
- Day +1: incident digest and anomalies summary
- Day +3: customer feedback triage and performance delta analysis
- Day +14: decision: keep prefetch.window=48 default or revert to conservative 24 based on cost/quality tradeoffs

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Smoke test script: GH:github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts/blob/main/patchwave_smoke.sh
- Rollback playbook: Confluence:Patchwave-Design-2027#rollback-playbook
- Telemetry dashboard: Grafana: dashboards/patchwave-weekly

---
Notes: this is a working draft. Expect edits after Monday preflight and after the first canary pass. Keep this doc as the canonical runbook for the week; update timestamps in the release channel.

Unresolved: need sign-off from finance for potential short bump in CPU minutes before Friday full roll.

End of doc.
